pages.x: Each spring the Franks held a great assembly, and each summer their king, Charles, called Charlemagne, Charles the Great, led his army out to war. In 46 years as king he fought more than fifty campaigns: against the Saxons, the Lombards, the Moors of Spain, the Bretons, the Avars and the Danes.

The pagan Saxons, in the forests of northern Germany, were the hardest enemy. In 772 Charlemagne cut down their sacred tree, the Irminsul. For thirty years they rose again and again, led for a time by a chieftain named Widukind, and Saxons were made to be baptised, on pain of death.

In 782 the Saxons wiped out a Frankish army. Charlemagne took his revenge at Verden, where, the royal annals say, 4,500 Saxon prisoners were beheaded in a single day. Widukind finally gave up and was baptised in 785, with Charlemagne as his godfather.
pages.of: Saxons beheaded in a day, the annals say

pages.x: In 773 the pope begged for help against the Lombards, who ruled northern Italy. Charlemagne crossed the Alps, besieged their capital, Pavia, through the winter, and in 774 made himself king of the Lombards. He sent their king to end his days in a monastery.

In 778, coming back from Spain, the rear of Charlemagne's army was ambushed by Basques in the mountain pass of Roncevaux, and every man was killed, among them a lord named Roland. Three centuries later The Song of Roland turned it into a heroic last stand against a Muslim army.

The Avars, horsemen from the steppe, held the plain of Hungary inside great ring-shaped fortresses. In 795 and 796 the Franks broke into their main ring and carried off its treasure, two centuries of plunder and tribute, said to have filled fifteen wagons drawn by oxen. The Avars never recovered.

On Christmas Day 800, in St Peter's in Rome, Pope Leo III set a crown on Charlemagne's head and hailed him as emperor, the first in the West for over three hundred years. His wars had united most of western Christendom, from northern Spain to the Elbe.

Charlemagne's empire was split among his grandsons in 843, and its western and eastern parts grew into France and Germany. His wars carried Christianity into Saxony, and his idea of a Christian empire in the West lived on in the Holy Roman Empire for a thousand years.
pts: More than fifty campaigns in 46 years
His empire was the seed of France and Germany
